title: I tried to land the replacement clause the T4 r6 critic left me, got it wrong, and stopped. Here is the dead end so nobody walks it again.
what_i_was_asked_to_do: The T4 r6 critic confirmed that round 4's gap-closure clause 1 is UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION on the character sheet, specified the exact replacement, and deliberately did not land it — CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 1 lets a critic ADD but never relax, the clause currently fails closed, and rewriting it makes it satisfiable, so landing it mid-round would be grading against an instrument it had just loosened. It recorded the patch verbatim and said the orchestrator may land it, because it bears on no filed score: it scored the sheet arm fail-closed exactly as it stands.
the_defect_being_repaired: `tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs`'s `rowProfile()` marks a column 'ink' if ANY pixel across the row's FULL height differs from the panel's modal colour. `game/src/ui/screens/progress.js:263` draws the character sheet's gauge trough at `gy = r[1] + 26*s, gw = r[2] - 56*s` — a second line BELOW the name/value text, spanning nearly the row's full width. So the gauge paints nearly every column, no run of >= 3 empty columns can exist, and `rows_with_fewer_than_two_separators: 0` cannot be satisfied on the sheet regardless of legibility. Level-up is genuinely different and must not move: `progress.js:135` puts its gauge at `gy = r[1] + 16*s` with its text baseline at `r[1] + 26*s`, i.e. side by side on one line, which is exactly what the clause was written to test.
what_i_tried_and_why_it_was_wrong: I tried to improve on the critic's patch by DERIVING the text band from the image instead of typing `20*s` and `26*s` in — find the gauge's top edge with the same green-plate predicate `t4-r4-critic.mjs` uses, and measure everything above it. The reasoning was the character work's 'stop typing z in' lesson: a constant copied out of `progress.js` goes stale the first time anybody re-pitches a row, which IS round 6's defect one layer out. Run against the stored T4-r4 captures, it found **0 gauge pixels on either screen** and was a silent no-op.
the_part_that_is_actually_my_failure: THE TOOL'S OWN HEADER ALREADY SAID THIS WOULD NOT WORK, AND I DID NOT READ IT BEFORE WRITING THE CODE. Lines 21-25 of `t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs`: *'A colour heuristic cannot: my first attempt classified glyph ink as dark-and-low-chroma and gauge as green. On the level-up screen the gauge plate is (42,55,43) and fails `G > B+12` by one unit; on the CHARACTER SHEET the panel's own ground is (44,57,45) — the same colour.'* The previous critic had already tried my idea, measured why it fails, and written it down at the top of the file I was editing. This is `CLAUDE.md` rule 0b in miniature: I acted on a general principle I remembered instead of reading the specific file in front of me, and the file was three lines from where I typed.
so_the_critics_typed_constants_are_RIGHT: A colour predicate cannot locate this gauge, because the trough and the panel ground are the same colour to within a unit. That leaves the source constants as the only available discriminator, which is what the critic specified. 'Never type a constant' is a good default and this is a measured exception — and the exception is documented in the instrument itself.
why_i_stopped_rather_than_landing_the_sp: The patch needs `s`, the UI scale, which the overlap tool does not carry and which I could not derive from the stored rects without guessing: the sheet's gauge ends at `34*s` by source arithmetic while the r4-era row rect is 32 px tall, so my derivation was already inconsistent, and round 5's reflow may have moved the pitch again. Verifying it needs a fresh capture of the CURRENT build, which is builder/critic work with a browser, not orchestrator work. Landing an unverified change to a CRITIC instrument is the exact shape this project keeps being burned by, so I reverted `tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs` to `HEAD` and left the clause failing closed, which is the safe direction.
who_should_do_it_and_what_they_need: The T4 round-7 critic, which will have live captures of the current build in hand. It needs: the sheet's row rect and the UI scale `s` from the same `getUIState()` report the rects come from, then `rowProfile` restricted to `[x, y, w, 26*s]` for `sheet` ONLY. Level-up must come back BIT-IDENTICAL — that is the required-to-disagree arm, and it is cheap. Note the clause becomes satisfiable once repaired, so per §1.3 guard 2 the critic that lands it may not use it as a reason to PASS.
one_thing_worth_keeping_from_the_dead_en: Running the OLD version of the tool from a scratchpad copy died instantly with an unresolved `../lib/cli.mjs` — a live confirmation of HAZARDS §22 from the other direction. §22 says a tool run from the main tree measures the main tree; the corollary is that a tool copied ANYWHERE ELSE does not run at all, because it resolves its own imports relative to itself. So the only way to run an old arm is a real worktree or a real clone with its own `tools/`, which is the same discipline §22 already demands.
